own_solution.law: For an ideal uniform string fixed at both ends, f1 = sqrt(T/mu)/(2L), with mu = m/L. Therefore f1 = sqrt(T/(mL))/2 = sqrt(100/(0.01 × 0.8))/2 = 55.9017 Hz.
assumptions: The usual flexible-string model for small transverse vibrations applies.
The target is the first, fully specified string.
The fixed supports maintain its vibrating length when its tension changes.

TC81D.regime: The applied tension is below the breaking threshold: T < q.

TA8BA.regime: The applied tension is below the stated capacity: T < q.

defect_reasons.other: After introducing the second string, references to 'the string' and 'this string' have an ambiguous antecedent, although the first, fully specified string is the natural intended target.

notes: The governing relation and all certified numerical answers check out. Tension increases of 9, 41 and 68 N give 58.3631, 66.3796 and 72.4569 Hz respectively. All listed breaking thresholds exceed 100 N. Cross-sectional area cancels through mu = rho A = [m/(AL)]A; converting mm² to m² consistently preserves this cancellation. Fixed endpoints support the claimed independence from the second string, and the earlier experiment does not replace the currently specified tension. Both declared minimal pairs retain the same number and unit while changing the intended event or object attachment. Each numeral-free control exactly replaces its numerical twin's '41 N' with 'small amount'; the authors do not claim equality of the unspecified increments. This resolves the pairing uncertainty noted in pass 1 without changing its physical conclusions. Outside the strength regime, a broken string has no corresponding intact-string fundamental mode; the packet explicitly excludes its reference expression from certification.
